title: OES-Resilience: Benchmarking telemetry intelligence under real-world stress
description:
Open, reproducible benchmark for multichannel telemetry anomaly detection. Synthetic 512-channel signals are split into sixteen 32-channel blocks and scored by block-level detectors behind a plugin API: the transparent OES32 reference detector (0.45·max|x| + 0.35·RMS + 0.20·mean|x|), a robust z-score baseline, EWMA and CUSUM temporal detectors, an oes32+ewma hybrid and an optional Isolation Forest, compared in a scorecard where every threshold is calibrated the same way on held-out clean data.

Version 0.5.0 adds a NASA SMAP/MSL adapter (the public data of Hundman et al. 2018 is downloaded with per-file SHA-256 verification and never bundled) and a blind evaluation on that real telemetry under a protocol locked and pushed before any test-split scoring. Every method gets the same standardised input and train-only thresholds. Result: OES32 did not meet its pre-stated success criterion. It was significantly better only than EWMA on SMAP, and the simpler max|x| baseline (both datasets) and CUSUM (MSL) reached a higher pooled event-level F1, although not significantly. Train-calibrated thresholds did not transfer to the test split for any method.

Version 0.4.0 added replay evaluation. A JSONL telemetry replay is scored against a hashed preregistration using the same detectors (plus a max|x| baseline). By default every threshold is calibrated to the shared ~1% false-positive budget on a hash-locked, event-free calibration replay, and fixed-threshold comparisons carry an explicit fairness note. Measured on the synthetic example: the calibrated CUSUM misses every event when applied to a regime-segmented replay.

Version 0.3.0 added a seeded stress suite with exact ground truth (heavy-tailed Student-t noise, missing channels, saturated and clipped channels, narrow and cross-block events, global shift plus burst, correlated blocks, slow drift and baseline steps) and robustness metrics relative to each detector's clean baseline (FP inflation, recall retention, 95% Wilson intervals). Missing data is handled explicitly with documented mask-aware scoring (no zero-filling). Measured weaknesses are reported: OES32 false positives rise sharply under heavy-tailed noise and it loses weak partial-block events, and the oes32+ewma hybrid does not beat EWMA alone.

The benchmark is synthetic; the only real data is the SMAP/MSL evaluation, which describes that dataset and protocol only. Not quantum, not GPS or navigation, not a physical sensor, and no performance claims about operational systems.
